title: Understanding MAE and MSE
text: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE) are both used to measure the accuracy of a model. However, they react differently to outliers. Consider how each metric calculates error and how they might be affected by large deviations.

title: MAE Calculation
text: MAE is calculated as the average of the absolute differences between predicted and actual values. It is given by the formula: $$MAE=\frac{\sum |y_i-y_{i,hat}|}{n}$$, where $$y_i$$ is the actual value, $$y_{i,hat}$$ is the predicted value, and $$n$$ is the number of observations.

title: MSE Calculation
text: MSE is calculated as the average of the squared differences between predicted and actual values. It is given by the formula: $$MSE=\frac{\sum \left(y_i-y_{i,hat}\right)^2}{n}$$. Consider how squaring the differences might affect sensitivity to outliers.

title: Sensitivity to Outliers
text: Outliers are data points that deviate significantly from other observations. Squaring the differences in MSE amplifies the impact of larger errors, making MSE more sensitive to outliers compared to MAE, which only takes the absolute value of differences.
